app.quit.what: Close the workbench, stopping firmware on the way out.
app.quit.answers: It answers before anything has closed, the quit running on its own goroutine, so a caller sees the reply and then the socket go. This is the one interface verb that does not refuse without an interface: a headless driver asking to quit means it, so firmware is stopped anyway and `headless` says that is what happened.

example.what: end the session, firmware and all

panels.list.what: Name every panel the interface has registered.
panels.list.answers: Every panel that exists, sorted, not the ones on screen: a panel nothing has opened is still named here, which is what makes this the list to choose a `panel.open` from. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: find out what there is to open

workspace.set.what: Show one of the workbench's top-level views.

params.name: view
params.what: the view's name, as panels.list and the view bar spell it

workspace.set.answers: Refuses when no interface is attached, and refuses a name that is not a view with the list of the ones that are.

example.what: go to the view that asks why one packet failed
